Of the 7,629 housing units in Mount Greenwood, 77 percent were built before 1970 and 9.9 percent before 1940, against a median build year of 1955. This is old-city housing, and it behaves like it: plaster, deep casing and a lot of coats already on the woodwork.

Count it by household and Mount Greenwood is 6,280 owning against 1,139 renting, 84.6 percent owner occupied. Count it by building and it is 84.1 percent detached, 1.6 percent attached, 12.6 percent in twos or more. Median unit: 6.6 rooms. Median value across that stock is $317,380.

Ranked against the 22 Chicago community areas covered here, Mount Greenwood lands in the top four on the highest owner-occupied share (84.6 percent, first of them all), the highest detached-house share (84.1 percent) and the largest homes by room count (6.6 rooms). It is also near the top for the highest median home value ($317,380).

Three figures put Mount Greenwood a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: townhomes and rowhouses at 1.6 percent against a 7.5 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 12.6 percent against a 29 percent average and prewar housing at 9.9 percent against a 15.8 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

How the age of the stock changes the work here

On stock with a 1955 median, the interior quote is decided by trim footage and not by wall area. 6.6 rooms is a lot of door casing, window casing and baseboard for the square footage, and every run of it is already carrying decades of paint. Original casing with sixty years on it prices very differently from casing that was stripped or replaced, which is the first thing worth establishing before anybody gives you a number. 6,280 households own in Mount Greenwood and 1,139 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

What should be on a written quote in Mount Greenwood

  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6.6 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.
  • Whole elevations. 84.1 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Distance, stated. Mount Greenwood is 5.7 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Mount Greenwood is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 77 percent of housing in Mount Greenwood was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar brick: bungalow, Cape Cod and the first generation of ranch. Little of the outside takes paint at all, so a Mount Greenwood exterior is soffit, fascia, overhangs, doors and the garage. Inside it is small rooms with a great deal of casing in them.

Two figures produce that sentence and no others: build year 1955, and a stock that is 84.1 percent detached, 1.6 percent attached and 12.6 percent in buildings of two or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Mount Greenwood is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Pre-1978 paint is the normal case in Mount Greenwood

The community-area tables stop at 1970 and never draw a 1978 line. What they give is 77 percent built before 1970, which is a floor rather than an answer, and no source puts a number on the gap for Mount Greenwood. Housing that old falls under the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, which covers any work disturbing paint in a home built before 1978. Illinois is not an authorized state for it, so EPA runs it here directly.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Mount Greenwood at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 6.6-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Mount Greenwood.

In Mount Greenwood it is worth asking about before the work starts rather than after the sanding has. Ask whoever you hire to say, in plain terms, how they intend to handle it at your particular address.

From the shop

Mount Greenwood is the most owner-occupied part of the city on this list, 84.6 percent, and it is a 1950s neighborhood in a literal sense: its median build year is 1955 and 84.1 percent of its housing is detached single-family. That is brick bungalow and Cape Cod stock, smaller rooms, a lot of door and window casing for the square footage, and very often a basement or attic that was finished later and painted to a different standard than the rest of the house. How is an interior price worked out for a house this size?

By trim, mostly. The median home in Mount Greenwood runs 6.6 rooms, and rooms bring door casing, window casing and baseboard with them. Wall area is the fast part of an interior job and trim is the slow part, so a quote that gives one number for the whole house is hiding the half of it that actually varies. Ask for the trim separately.

Mount Greenwood is 5.7 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip.
